<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.35pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Accounting for Long-Lived Assets and Impairment Charges</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Long-lived assets are reviewed for impairment
whenever events or circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of the asset
may not be recoverable.&#160; If the sum of
the expected future cash flows (undiscounted and without interest charges) from
an asset to be held and used in operations is less than the carrying value of
the asset, an impairment loss must be recognized in the amount of the
difference between the carrying value and the fair value of the assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have a policy of reviewing the financial
operations of our restaurant locations on at least a quarterly basis.&#160; Locations that are not meeting expectations
are identified and continue to be monitored closely throughout the year.&#160; Primarily in the fourth quarter, we review
actual results and budgets for the ensuing year are analyzed.&#160; If we deem that a location&#146;s results will
continue to be below expectations, we consider alternatives for its continued
operation.&#160; At that time, we perform
asset impairment testing.&#160; If it is
determined that the fair value of an asset is greater than its carrying value,
an impairment charge is recorded.&#160; Upon a
triggering event such as a formal decision for abandonment (restaurant
closure), we may record additional impairment of assets, including an
allocation of goodwill. Any carryover basis of assets is depreciated over the
respective remaining useful lives.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair value of assets is determined primarily on the
likelihood of future use of the assets through operations or by the value that
could be received for the asset if sold.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other charges include write-offs of allocated
goodwill, severance costs, lease and contract termination fees, professional
service costs, and settlement of litigation. During fiscal years 2004, 2003,
and 200, we recorded asset impairment charges and other as follows (in
thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The long-lived asset impairment amount in the table
above represents the net book value of the fixed assets that will not be
recovered through regular operations, computed on a discounted cash flow
basis.&#160; The amount in 2004 is
attributable primarily to the impairment of one Bamboo Club location.&#160; The amount in 2003 is attributable primarily
to impairments of two Bamboo Club locations and the closure of one Redfish
location.&#160; The amount in 2002 is
attributable primarily of impairments related to six TGI Friday&#146;s locations;
three not yet built Bamboo Club locations; and one Redfish location.</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3.</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>INCOME TAXES</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December 27, 2004, we had approximately
$12,800,000 federal net operating and tax credit carryforwards to be used to
offset future income for federal income tax purposes.&#160; These carryforwards expire in the years 2011
to 2023. The net change in the total valuation allowance for the year ended
December 27, 2004 and December 29, 20023, is the result of providing a full
valuation allowance against all deferred tax assets because of the significant
loss in 2002 and 2003.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We had a $15 million

<p align="left" style="line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;text-autospace:none;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All of our loan agreements contain various financial
covenants that are generally measured at the end of each calendar quarter.&#160; There are two key covenants we must
meet.&#160; One loan agreement requires a</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-20</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">cash
flow coverage test, which requires us to produce a level of earnings before
interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization and other unusual gains or
losses (EBITDA) in excess of the next 12 months amount of the principal and
interest under our debt obligations.&#160;
Other loan agreements modify this covenant for items such as pre-opening
costs and rent expense, making it more of a fixed charge coverage test.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Another covenant restricts the aggregate amount of
total senior debt we can have to a multiple of EBITDA.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

covenants, as amended, for all debt agreements.&#160;
All long-term debt is secured by certain assets of various restaurant
locations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">6.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; STOCKHOLDERS&#146;
EQUITY</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Stock
Options</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have an Incentive Stock Option Plan (the &#147;2002
Plan&#148;) that provides for the issuance of options to acquire up to 1,000,000
shares of our common stock.&#160; The options
are intended to qualify as incentive stock options within the meaning of
Section 422A of the Internal Revenue Code or as options which are not intended
to meet the requirements of such section (&#147;non-qualified stock options&#148;).&#160; Awards granted under the 2002 Plan also may
include stock appreciation rights and restricted stock awards.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The exercise price of all incentive stock
options granted under the 2002 Plan must be at least equal to the fair market
value of such shares as of the date of grant or, in the case of incentive stock
options granted to a holder of 10% or more of the our common stock, at least
110% of the fair market value of such shares on the date of grant.&#160; The plan administrator (currently the Board
of Directors) sets the term of each stock option, but
no incentive stock option may be exercisable more than 10 years after the date
such option is granted.&#160; We also have
granted options under the 1990, 1995, and 1999 Incentive Stock Option Plans,
all of which contain similar terms to the 2002 Plan.</font></p>

<p style="line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On June 17, 2003, we issued approximately 291,250
options to directors, management, and key employees with an exercise price of
$2.17 per share, the fair market value of our common stock on the date of
grant.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are also authorized to issue or have outstanding
options under all of our unexpired stock option plans.&#160; During 2004, we issued 22,500 stock options.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A summary of the status of our stock option plans at
December 27, 2004, December 29, 2003, and December 30, 2002, and changes during
the years then ended is presented in the table below:</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Common
Stock Warrants</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December 29, 2003, we had 231,277 outstanding
warrants to acquire our common stock with our lenders in connection with the
issuances of previously paid-off debt.&#160;
These warrants expired in March 2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">7.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; COMMITMENTS
AND CONTINGENCIES</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Development Agreements</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are obligated under separate development
agreements with TGI Friday&#146;s Inc. to open 16 new TGI Friday&#146;s restaurants
through 2009.&#160; The development agreements
give TGI Friday&#146;s Inc. certain remedies in the event we fail to timely comply
with the development agreements, including the right, under certain
circumstances, to terminate our exclusive rights to develop restaurants in the
related franchised territory.&#160; Our
development territories include most of Arizona, Nevada, New Mexico, Southern
California, and the El Paso metropolitan areas.&#160;
We anticipate building three to four new TGI Fridays during 2005 and we
are currently negotiating for two new TGI Friday&#146;s restaurant sites for 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Franchise, License, and Marketing Agreements</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with the terms of the TGI Friday&#146;s
restaurant franchise agreements, we are required to pay franchise fees of
$50,000 ($25,000 for our Southern California locations) for each restaurant
opened.&#160; We also are required to pay a
royalty of up to 4% of gross sales, although we have entered into California
Development Incentive Agreement which will reduce a portion of these fees.&#160; Royalty expense was approximately $7,510,000,
$7,476,000, and $7,444,000 under these agreements during 2003, 2002, and 2001,
respectively.&#160; In addition, we could be
required to spend up to 4% of gross sales on marketing.&#160; Marketing expense for TGI Friday&#146;s restaurant
locations under these agreements was approximately $6,195,000, $5,250,000, and
$4,772,000 during 2004, 2003, and 2002, respectively.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-22</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Operating Leases</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We lease land and restaurant facilities under
operating leases having terms (including option periods) expiring at various
dates through October 2022.&#160; The
restaurant leases have from two to three renewal clauses of five years each at
our option, and have provisions for contingent rentals based upon a percentage
of gross sales.&#160; Our minimum future lease
payments as of December 27, 2004, were as follows (in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Rent expense during 2004, 2003, and 2002 was
approximately $12.3 million, $12.5 million (as restated), and $12.1 million (as
restated), respectively.&#160; In addition, we
paid contingent rentals of $840,000, $958,000, and $1,061,000 during 2004,
2003, and 2002, respectively.&#160; The
difference between rent expense and rent paid due to recording expenses on the
straight-line method is included in other liabilities and deferred credits in
the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Contingencies</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:9.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the normal course of business, we are named as a
defendant in various claims and litigation matters.&#160; From time
to time, we are subject to routine contract, negligence, employment related,
and other litigation in the ordinary course of business.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are involved in two
lawsuits filed on behalf of current employees, seeking damages, under
California law, for both missed breaks and missed meal breaks the employees
allege they did not receive. These lawsuits seek to establish a class action
relating to our California operations. We intend to vigorously defend these
lawsuits, both on the merits of the employees&#146; cases and the issues relating to
class action status.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;The state of California initiated a sales tax
audit of our restaurants and determined that the optional 15% gratuity added to
checks for parties of eight or more should have been subject to sales tax and,
as such, has assessed taxes and related penalties of initially approximately
$900,000, but which have since been reduced to approximately $484,000.&#160; We have vigorously contested this assessment.
The first of various appeal conferences was held on November 13, 2003.&#160; In February 2004, we were notified that our
appeal was denied by the appeals officer.&#160;
We are in the process of preparing a second appeal to the full state of
California Franchise Tax Board. We are unable to predict the outcome of this
proceeding.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other than the preceding, we
are not subject to any pending litigation that we believe will have a material
adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations, or
liquidity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are also subject, from time to time, to audit by
various taxing authorities reviewing our income, property, sales, use, and
payroll taxes.&#160; We believe that any
finding from such audits will not have a material impact on our financial
condition, results of operations, or liquidity.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

PLANS</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We maintain a 401(k) Savings Plan for all of our
employees.&#160; We currently match 50% of the
participants&#146; contributions up to the first 4%.&#160;
Contributions made by us were approximately $234,000, $235,000, and
$257,000, during 2004, 2003, and 2002, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">9.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; SUBSEQUENT
EVENTS</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subsequent
to the year ended December 27, 2004, we completed negotiations and entered into
an agreement with the landlord of the Bamboo Club in Aventura, FL, to terminate
the lease and we closed this restaurant on February 24, 2005.&#160; We also completed negotiations and entered
into an agreement with the landlord of the Bamboo Club in Newport, KY to
terminate the lease and to close this restaurant on May 31, 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additionally,
we completed negotiations and entered into an agreement with the landlord in Columbus
OH, where we had not yet built a restaurant, to terminate the lease.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In
February 2005, we paid $575,000 in lease termination fees for Aventura, FL and
Columbus OH.</font></p>
